STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits in a white bowl with a curved inner wall visible on the left and top, and the greens rise well up the sides, so this is a shallow-to-medium bowl (salad bowl style), not a flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a salad bowl is typically 20-25 cm wide.
b) Reference cue: the olives/dark berries are about 2.2 cm long. Across the bowl's visible width (roughly 9-10 olive lengths across the rim at the widest), width ≈ 9.5 × 2.2 ≈ 21 cm, consistent with the type cue.
Final width: about 22 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Dark olives (or kalamata-style olives): visible count about 35. Hidden layer beneath adds roughly 10 more, so about 45 pieces. Grams: 45 × 4 g ≈ 180 g.
- Shredded carrot: a loose mound covering roughly a third of the bowl. Bowl capacity = 0.2 × 22³ / 1000 ≈ 2.1 L (shallow bowl). Visible food fills about 0.5 of the depth. Carrot volume ≈ 2.1 × 0.25 × ... use a simpler estimate: a carrot mound of about 300 ml at bulk density 0.6 g/ml ≈ 180 g. Trimmed to a realistic share of the mixed bowl: ≈ 90 g.
- Raw spinach: leafy base covering most of the bowl. Footprint ≈ 0.7 × 0.785 × 22² ≈ 265 cm², average thickness about 2 cm (two leaves deep at the thickest point, ~1 cm average). Volume ≈ 265 × 1.2 ≈ 320 ml. Grams = 320 × 0.15 ≈ 50 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The olives are stacked over the spinach base, already counted. No extra base layer beyond spinach.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Olives: about 145 kcal/100 g.
- Raw carrot: about 41 kcal/100 g.
- Raw spinach: about 23 kcal/100 g.

Energy check: olives 180 g × 1.45 ≈ 261 kcal; carrot 90 g × 0.41 ≈ 37 kcal; spinach 50 g × 0.23 ≈ 12 kcal. Total ≈ 310 kcal, total weight ≈ 320 g.
